newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to crack down on tax dodgers.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to crack down on tax dodgers.

text.p: The Lithuanian government is planning a crackdown on big companies and large retailers who are dodging paying taxes, Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday.
"We want to warn companies...in the next few days we will launch a severe action against those who deliberately avoid paying taxes," Vagnorius told a news conference.
Vagnorius said strict punishments will be applied for keeping goods without the necessary documents, manipulating cash registers or double book-keeping.
Tax collection has been a major headache for governments all over eastern Europe as new systems of registering for tax and filing tax returns are introduced.
VAT is also a key source of revenue and one that many businesses seek to evade.
"An instruction has been issued to start checking the most powerful and strongest companies and shops and those who avoid paying taxes in the most blatant way," Vagnorius said.

Vagnorius said he expected that the action, which will be launched across the whole country, will improve revenue collection in March and will allow the government to continue reforming its tax administration.
The highest fines for avoiding paying taxes will be as high as two million litas or imprisonment.
The government hopes for VAT revenues of 3.425 billion litas in 1997 and has planned a 1997 budget deficit of 697 million litas.
